utility.notes: Del Mar is a well-documented San Diego County city within SDG&E's core service territory, consistent with SDG&E-territory records established elsewhere this session.

value.name: Clean Energy Alliance (CEA)
value.notes: CEA's own homepage confirms Del Mar as one of its 7 member cities (Carlsbad, Del Mar, Escondido, Oceanside, San Marcos, Solana Beach, Vista) — Carlsbad, Del Mar, and Solana Beach were CEA's founding cities in 2019. Per CEA's own description: 'Clean Energy Alliance purchases power directly from power providers and/or builds energy generation sources' while 'SDG&E delivers energy, handles billing and serves customers.'

permit_authority.value: City of Del Mar Building Services

permit_url.notes: The city's general Building Services page does not itself contain solar-specific content; no dedicated solar permit page was located this session.

interconnection_url.notes: SDG&E's own utility-wide Net Energy Metering (NEM) interconnection page, already established for other SDG&E-territory records this session.

value.name: SGIP - Residential Solar and Storage Equity
value.administrator: Center for Sustainable Energy (CSE), on behalf of SDG&E, under the CPUC's Self-Generation Incentive Program
value.description: Storage incentive of $1,100/kWh paired with a solar incentive of $3,100/kW, funded via a $280 million CPUC-authorized statewide budget that opened for reservations June 2, 2025 and remains an active program per SGIP's own statewide announcements (most recently dated 2026-07-23). Administered across SDG&E's entire distribution territory, which includes Del Mar/San Diego County.
value.eligibility: PG&E, SCE, or SDG&E residential customers (general market tier)

battery_programs.notes: Reused as a utility-level fact already established for other IOU-territory records this session: the CPUC-administered SGIP program applies uniformly across the named utility's entire distribution territory, directly verified via SGIP's own site (selfgenca.com) / the CPUC's own SGIP program page, including a program-status announcement as recent as 2026-07-23 confirming the program remains active.

value.name: Eligibility Checklist (per City of Del Mar Municipal Code Section 23.21.050(C))
Standard engineering evaluation verifying the support structure is adequate for wind/seismic/dead/live loads
Verification the existing electrical system (line, load, ground, bonding, panel/subpanel sizing) can carry the new PV load

required_documents.notes: Per Del Mar Municipal Code Section 23.21.050 (Applications and Documents).

value: Call (858) 375-9528 or email Inspector@delmar.ca.us to request an inspection
Inspection requests are available Monday-Friday (except City holidays); call the inspection line by 4:00pm to schedule an inspection for the next day
inspection_steps.notes: This is the City's general Building Division inspection-request process (the same page covers all building permit types, including solar); the City does not publish a separate, solar-specific inspection sequence.

value.program_or_pathway: Expedited Small Residential Rooftop Solar Systems permitting (Del Mar Municipal Code Ch. 23.21)
other_conditions: System must be installed on a single- or duplex-family dwelling
Solar panel/module array must not exceed the maximum legal building height as defined by the City
Only one consolidated inspection is required for eligible systems (may combine with the Fire Marshal)
Approval does not itself authorize grid interconnection; the applicant must separately obtain the local utility provider’s approval
